title: Random forest on serum proteomics separates psoriatic from rheumatoid arthritis
summary: Serum proteomes of early inflammatory arthritis patients were measured by mass spectrometry, SomaScan and Luminex, and multivariate machine learning separated psoriatic from rheumatoid arthritis with AUC 0.94 (nano-LC-MS/MS), 0.69 (bead immunoassay) and 0.73 (aptamer assay) in discovery. Random forest models on proteins measured by multiple reaction monitoring reached AUCs of 0.79 and 0.85 in verification and an independent cohort of 167 patients. The authors note a need for larger cohorts including other arthropathies.
ai_technology: Random forest and multivariate machine learning on multi-platform serum proteomics

evidence.tested: Discovery (n=60 for MRM) and independent cohort evaluation (n=167) with multiple reaction monitoring assays.
evidence.unknown: Modest AUCs; small discovery cohorts; other arthropathies not tested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest models selected and combined proteins to discriminate the two diagnoses.
